_comment: Holidays kept across Tamriel as a whole, plus Skyrim's own.
DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE to add your own events. Every *.json in this
folder is loaded and merged, so add a file of your own instead; it
will survive updates to this one.
Every entry carries a stable "id", so another file can override or
remove any of them by reusing that id. See 00_README.txt.
For the holidays of individual provinces -- High Rock, Hammerfell,
Elsweyr and the rest -- add the optional 20_Provinces.json.

events.name: New Life Festival
events.description: The year opens with feasting across Tamriel. Every tavern offers free drink, and no work is done.

events.name: South Wind's Prayer
events.description: A plea by all the religions of Tamriel for a good planting season. The temples perform free healings for the few judged worthy.

events.name: Feast of the Dead
events.description: Celebrated vigorously by the Nords of Windhelm. The names of Ysgramor's Five Hundred Companions are recited during a great feast to honor the Return.

events.name: Heart's Day
events.description: Lovers exchange gifts in memory of Polydor and Eloisa. Innkeepers across Tamriel offer a free room to travellers.

events.name: First Planting
events.description: The seeds of the autumn harvest are symbolically sown. A festival of fresh beginnings: neighbours reconcile, bad habits are dropped, and the temples run a free clinic all day.

events.name: Jester's Day
events.description: Pranks are set up from one end of town to the other, and even the most dignified councilman might attempt a joke. Watch your purse.

events.name: Second Planting
events.description: As First Planting, but for the soul as much as the soil. The temples open their free clinics for the second and last time this year.

events.name: Mid Year Celebration
events.description: The height of summer, and the traditional midpoint of the year. The temples offer their blessings for half the usual donation.

events.name: Merchants' Festival
events.description: Every marketplace and equipment store drops its prices. The bargain shoppers of the known world are out in force.

events.name: Sun's Rest
events.description: Every shop is closed and the day is given over to rest rather than commerce. The Merchants' Guild fines any shop that stays open.

events.name: Harvest's End
events.description: The seeding, sowing and reaping are done. The taverns offer free drink all day and even visitors are invited to join the farmers.

events.name: Tales and Tallows
events.description: The dead are said to walk tonight. The superstitious keep silent for fear of possession, while the Mages Guild celebrates the oldest magical science and halves the price of every enchanted item.

events.name: The Burning of King Olaf
events.description: Solitude burns an effigy of High King Olaf One-Eye, condemned in ancient verse as a tyrant. The Bards College oversees this fiery celebration of Solitude's history.

events.name: Witches' Festival
events.description: Sorcery and religion clash. Conjurers and warlocks meet in the wilds beyond the cities, and what they summon there may trouble Tamriel for years. Wise folk stay indoors.

events.name: The Emperor's Birthday
events.description: Historically celebrating the Septim rulers, this day is now kept by Imperial loyalists to honor Emperor Titus Mede II. Travelling carnivals entertain the masses while the aristocracy hunts.

events.name: Warriors' Festival
events.description: Weapons are half price and every warrior, spellsword and rogue is at the smithy. Quiet streets ring with the skirmishes of boys who have just bought a first sword.

events.name: North Wind's Prayer
events.description: A thanksgiving to the gods for a good harvest and a mild winter. The temples offer blessing, curing and healing for half the usual donation.

events.name: Saturalia
events.description: Originally a holiday for a forgotten god of debauchery, Saturalia has evolved into Tamriel's major winter revel -- a time of gift-giving, festive clothing, and parading.

events.name: Old Life Festival
events.description: The last day of the year, spent in the temples reflecting on the one behind. It is rumoured the priests perform their final resurrections of the year without charge.
